description: Given the root of a complete binary tree, return the number of nodes. A complete binary tree has every level fully filled except possibly the last, which is filled from left to right. Design an algorithm that runs in less than O(n) time complexity.
intuition: In a complete binary tree, either the left or right subtree is a perfect binary tree. Compare subtree heights: if equal, the left is perfect (count its nodes with 2^h - 1 + 1 and recurse right). If unequal, the right is perfect at one level shorter. This gives O(log^2 n) time.
approach: Compare the left and right subtree heights. If equal, the left subtree is a perfect binary tree with 2^h - 1 nodes plus the root. Recurse on the right. If unequal, the right subtree is perfect, recurse on the left.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: root = [1,2,3,4,5,6] (complete binary tree)

Tree structure:
      1
     / \
    2   3
   / \ /
  4  5 6

countNodes(root=1):
  leftHeight: 1->2->4 = 3
  rightHeight: 1->3 = 2 (no right child of 3)
  leftHeight(3) != rightHeight(2) -> recurse
  return 1 + countNodes(2) + countNodes(3)

countNodes(node=2):
  leftHeight: 2->4 = 2
  rightHeight: 2->5 = 2
  leftHeight === rightHeight = 2 -> perfect tree
  return (1 << 2) - 1 = 4 - 1 = 3

countNodes(node=3):
  leftHeight: 3->6 = 2
  rightHeight: 3 (no right) = 1
  heights differ -> recurse
  return 1 + countNodes(6) + countNodes(null)
  countNodes(6): leftH=1, rightH=1 -> (1<<1)-1=1
  countNodes(null): 0
  return 1 + 1 + 0 = 2

Total: 1 + 3 + 2 = 6

Output: 6
explanation:
1. Compute left height (going all left) and right height (going all right).
2. If equal, the tree is perfect: return 2^h - 1.
3. If not equal, recurse on both subtrees plus 1 for root.
4. In each recursion, one subtree will be perfect, so only one path recurses.
5. This gives O(log^2 n) time complexity.
hints: A complete binary tree has a special structure you can exploit.
Compare left and right heights to determine if a subtree is perfect.
A perfect binary tree of height h has 2^h - 1 nodes.
